title: ID0418778-DC/Si-D/FR-[MP/R4 170001749] Cable pins damaged
description:
Reported behavior/issue:
I would like to report a new issue observed on one of our charging
cables. One of the pins appears to be slightly coming out of its
socket, which may indicate a defect or damage.
Could you please advise on the following points:
1. Is this a known issue, or has it been reported before?
2. Could this potentially be linked to other recent issues we’ve
experienced (e.g., abnormal fan behavior, sensor alerts, etc.)?
3. What are the recommended next steps (e.g., replacement,
further inspection)?
Pictures can be provided if needed.
Looking forward to your feedback.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0418778-DC/Si-D/FR-[MP/R4170001749] Cable pins damaged CRM:02679000112
additional_info.body:
Dear Mura Florian,
I hope you’re doing well.
As you mentioned, and based on the picture provided, it appears that the pins appear to be slightly coming out of its
socket, which may indicate a defect or damage. There is a risk of melting or more damaged when charging a vehicle, so as a safety measure, we recommend disabling the affected outlet until further troubleshooting can be performed.
For further analysis, if you have the following information available, could you please share it with us?
On which outlet is the issue observed—DC1 or DC2?
The total kWh delivered and an estimate of the number of charging sessions on this outlet.
Is a CMS (Charge Management System) installed?
A picture of the plug type label.
We thank you for your time and patience in advance.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Abhinav Malokar

change
the
subject of this Email when
replying
to it.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0418778-DC/Si-D/FR-[MP/R4170001749] Cable pins damaged CRM:02679000112
additional_info.body:
Dear Team,
As mentioned by the customer and based on the picture provided, it appears that the pins are slightly protruding from their socket, which may indicate a defect or potential damage. This poses a risk of melting or further damage during vehicle charging.
As a safety precaution, we recommend disabling the affected outlet until further troubleshooting can be carried out. Additionally, please plan for a site intervention to perform a physical inspection of the connector and surrounding components.
Adding to that, upon reviewing similar cases, it was noted that the customer has already discussed this topic with the French team. Therefore, for the further course of action, we are moving this ticket accordingly.
